title: Mechanical Watch Foundations
description: The whole movement first: power, train, winding, setting. Escapements and complications wait until the simple calibre is thinkable.

sourceReferences.title: HSNY Horology 101–103
sourceReferences.notes: 101 movement mechanics before 102 gear train before 103 winding/setting. Escapement is 104. Complications are not in the beginner ladder.

sourceReferences.title: WOSTEP training and education
sourceReferences.notes: Theory and component work before chronometry and chronograph as later specializations.

modules.title: The whole movement
modules.blurb: A machine that counts the unwind of a spring.
learningObjectives: Name the stored work, train, escapement, and display of a movement
Take a simple movement down and put it back without losing location

modules.title: Power and the going train
learningObjectives: Trace power from mainspring through the going train to the escape wheel
Compute beat rate from tooth counts instead of treating 28,800 as a slogan

modules.title: Winding and setting
modules.blurb: How energy gets in and how the hands get moved.
learningObjectives: Wind the spring and set the hands through the keyless works
Keep oil in the right place and endshake inside freedom, not rattle

concepts.name: A mechanical watch as a machine
concepts.summary: Stored work, a train, an escapement, a display.
objectives: Name stored work, train, escapement, and display as the four jobs of a movement
Trace power through the train, and say how the oscillator regulates that train rather than driving the hands

concepts.name: Naming the parts
concepts.summary: Plate, bridge, wheel, pinion, jewel — the words the rest of the course uses.
objectives: Name plate, bridge, wheel, pinion, and jewel so later lessons have words
Point at those parts on a simple calibre instead of waving at 'the movement'

concepts.name: The bench
concepts.summary: A movement holder and the discipline of not losing a screw.
objectives: Hold a movement so a screw cannot roll and a pivot cannot bend
Name the discipline of the bench before any complication arrives

concepts.name: Plates and bridges
concepts.summary: The frame everything else is located in.
objectives: Treat plates and bridges as the frame that locates every pivot
Predict what a distorted bridge does to endshake and mesh

concepts.name: Jewels as bearings
concepts.summary: Hard, polished holes that reduce friction.
objectives: Describe a jewel as a hard, polished hole that reduces friction
Predict why a dry or cracked jewel is a timing and wear problem

concepts.name: Taking down a simple movement
concepts.summary: Order matters. So does putting it back.
objectives: Take a simple movement down in an order you can reverse
Predict the part that jumps or scores if the order is wrong

concepts.name: Hands as a display
concepts.summary: The hands are not the timebase.
objectives: Treat the hands as a display, not the timebase
Predict what setting the hands must not do to the oscillator

concepts.name: The mainspring
concepts.summary: A spiral of steel that stores work.
objectives: Describe the mainspring as a spiral that stores work
Predict what a set or tired spring does to torque through the day

concepts.name: The barrel
concepts.summary: The drum that holds the spring and drives the first wheel.
objectives: Name the barrel as the drum that holds the spring and drives the first wheel
Trace torque from arbor to barrel wall to the centre pinion

concepts.name: The going train
concepts.summary: A reduction from the barrel to the escape wheel.
objectives: Follow a reduction from the barrel to the escape wheel
State why the train counts and does not keep time

concepts.name: Wheels and pinions
concepts.summary: A large wheel driving a small pinion, over and over.
objectives: Describe a large wheel driving a small pinion, over and over
Predict backlash and wear if the mesh is too deep or too shallow

concepts.name: Gear ratios and beat
concepts.summary: Tooth counts decide how often the escapement ticks.
objectives: Read tooth counts as the reason the escapement ticks at a chosen rate
Compute a simple train ratio from wheel and pinion teeth

concepts.name: Tooth counts as a calculation
concepts.summary: Why 18,000 and 28,800 are not slogans.
objectives: Show why 18,000 and 28,800 beats per hour fall out of tooth counts
Predict the beat rate if one wheel in the train changes teeth

concepts.name: Beat rate
concepts.summary: Beats per hour as the movement's clock.
objectives: Define beat rate as beats per hour, the movement's clock
Relate beat rate to the oscillator period, not to the case size

concepts.name: Power reserve
concepts.summary: How long the spring can run the train.
objectives: State power reserve as how long the spring can run the train
Predict what extra friction or a thicker oil does to that number

concepts.name: Click and ratchet
concepts.summary: The one-way that keeps the spring from unwinding through the crown.
objectives: Name the click and ratchet as the one-way that keeps the spring wound
Predict what a failed click does the moment you let go of the crown

concepts.name: Winding
concepts.summary: Putting work back into the spring.
objectives: Put work back into the spring through the winding path
Trace the clutch position that connects crown to ratchet

concepts.name: Stem and crown
concepts.summary: The shaft the wearer actually turns.
objectives: Name the stem and crown as the shaft the wearer actually turns
Predict what a loose stem does to winding and setting

concepts.name: Setting the hands
concepts.summary: Decoupling the display from the timebase.
objectives: Decouple the display from the timebase so the hands can be set
Predict whether the oscillator should keep running while you set

concepts.name: Keyless works
concepts.summary: The clutch that chooses wind versus set.
objectives: Describe keyless works as the clutch that chooses wind versus set
Trace pull-out positions to the sliding pinion

concepts.name: Cannon pinion and motion works
concepts.summary: Hour and minute as a 12:1 reduction.
objectives: Read hour and minute as a 12:1 reduction at the cannon pinion
Predict a jumping minute if the cannon slips on the centre arbor

concepts.name: Motion works versus going train
concepts.summary: Two trains, two jobs.
objectives: Distinguish the motion works from the going train by job
Predict which train a date disc should take power from

concepts.name: Lubrication
concepts.summary: The right oil in the right place, and nowhere else.
objectives: Put the right oil in the right place and nowhere else
Predict what oil on an escape-tooth locking face does to the rate

concepts.name: Endshake and freedom
concepts.summary: A pivot that must move, but not rattle.
objectives: Leave a pivot free to turn without rattle
Diagnose a bound or noisy train from too little or too much endshake
